versions.name: RXV2-0.9.692-goblin-detail
versions.notes: The 3D helicopter is a proper model now. The nose bulge is gone - the whole shell is one smooth surface instead of spheres stuck together - and the front is shorter. The canopy stops behind the cabin, so you can see the black carbon frame, the motor, the servos and the battery, just as you can on the real thing. The boom carries GOBLIN lettering and a tail stabiliser, and the tail fin is swept rather than a square slab. Includes 0.9.691.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.691-goblin-livery
versions.notes: The 3D helicopter now looks like a real model helicopter: orange shell with the white and black graphics, white boom and skids, orange tail fin, and a blunt rounded nose instead of the sharp cone. It also has two blades, as a Goblin does, rather than four. Includes 0.9.690.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.690-heli-3d
versions.notes: The rotating helicopter on the View channels page is much better looking. It now sits on a real shadow, the bodywork is glossy and catches the light, the metal parts look like metal, and you can see through the spinning rotor instead of it being a grey plate. Same model, properly lit. Includes 0.9.689.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.689-dev-host
versions.notes: The built-in address for a local firmware server was the developer's own Mac name. Two reasons to change it: it published a private machine name in every release, and any computer on your network answering to that name could have offered your receiver firmware. It is now a neutral name that nothing answers to by default, so updates come from messiter.com unless you set your own. Includes 0.9.688.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.688-usb-advice
versions.notes: Three pages still told you to turn the USB socket on in Setup - a button that 0.9.687 removed, because the receiver now works the socket out for itself. They now say to restart the receiver, which is the only thing that can actually be wrong. Found in an App Store screenshot. Includes 0.9.687.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.687-fewer-settings
versions.notes: Two settings left the Setup menu, because the receiver already knows the answers. It works out for itself whether it is a dongle or a receiver, and a flight controller plugged into its USB socket is adopted with no setting to turn on. A board that IS a dongle still shows its own button for the name and serial speed, and that is also where a receiver whose radios failed to start can force itself back to being a receiver. Also: in the new-helicopter wizard, the Back up step opened the Setup page instead of Backup & restore. Includes 0.9.686.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.686-log-colour
versions.notes: The Receiver log button at the foot of Black box was grey, which reads as disabled. It is now the Receiver log's own blue - bright, and clear of the green above it. Includes 0.9.685.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.685-button-gap
versions.notes: Read black box: the two buttons touched - the link above had no bottom margin and the button below had none at all. Checked by screenshot this time, not by reading the CSS. Includes 0.9.684.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.684-read-black-box
versions.notes: The Vibration check is now called READ BLACK BOX, because that is what it does - it grew from filter advice into the whole flight - and it lives inside the black box area instead of as a separate entry in the list. Black box (Flight recorder) leads with it, and the Receiver log sits at the foot of the same page, so everything about recordings is in one place. Includes 0.9.683.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.683-log-under-blackbox
versions.notes: The Receiver log is offered plainly at the foot of Black box (Flight recorder) - no heading, no explaining - and is off the front page. It reappears on the front page only for a receiver with no Rotorflight, which would otherwise have no Black box page to reach it through. Includes 0.9.682.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.682-receiver-log
versions.notes: Two things were both called the black box. The receiver's own is now the RECEIVER LOG - what this receiver saw: live status, the radio link, past flights and events - on the front page, in its title and help, and in search. Black box (Flight recorder) keeps that name for the flight controller's recording, and now carries a 'Not this one?' card pointing across to the Receiver log; the Receiver log points back. Includes 0.9.681.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.681-black-box
versions.notes: Rotorflight's Flight recorder is now called Black box (Flight recorder), and sits under B in the a-la-carte list where you look for it. The page, its help and everything that points at it say Black box; the search index keeps both meanings apart, since the receiver has a Black box page of its own. Includes 0.9.680.
